blocks.en: Labs that grow Arabidopsis in liquid medium usually improvise the setup with foam cut to size, mesh taped over a container, or a fixed plate above a reservoir. None of it repeats between labs, or even between runs in one lab.
blocks.text: Labs that grow Arabidopsis in liquid medium usually improvise the setup with foam cut to size, mesh taped over a container, or a fixed plate above a reservoir. None of it repeats between labs, or even between runs in one lab.
blocks.zh: 以液態培養液栽培Arabidopsis的實驗室，多半自行拼湊裝置：切成大小的泡棉、用膠帶固定在容器上的網子，或是架在水槽上方的固定板。這些做法在不同實驗室之間無法重現，甚至同一間實驗室的不同次試驗之間也不一致。

blocks.en: This plate floats on the medium, so the seedlings stay at the same depth however much liquid is left. It is three print files for a standard FDM printer, so another lab can print the same plate and grow seedlings at the same depth and spacing.
blocks.text: This plate floats on the medium, so the seedlings stay at the same depth however much liquid is left. It is three print files for a standard FDM printer, so another lab can print the same plate and grow seedlings at the same depth and spacing.
blocks.zh: 這塊板子浮在培養液上，因此不論液體剩下多少，幼苗都停在同一深度。它是三個供一般 FDM 列印機使用的列印檔，所以別的實驗室可以印出同一塊板子，在相同的深度與間距下栽培幼苗。

blocks.en: The first version was a fixed plate over a liquid chamber, so the level of the medium had to be set by hand before every run.
blocks.text: The first version was a fixed plate over a liquid chamber, so the level of the medium had to be set by hand before every run.
blocks.zh: 最初的版本是架在液槽上方的固定板，因此每次試驗前都得用手把培養液的液位調好。

blocks.en: The level has to sit just under the plate, as high as possible. Too low and the roots lose contact; too high and the plate floods. The window is narrow.
blocks.text: The level has to sit just under the plate, as high as possible. Too low and the roots lose contact; too high and the plate floods. The window is narrow.
blocks.zh: 液位必須剛好落在板子下方，而且盡可能高。太低，根會失去接觸；太高，板子會被淹過。可用的區間很窄。

blocks.en: The level also moves. The plants drink and the medium evaporates, so a level set at the start of a run is wrong by the end. Every top-up lets conditions drift between replicates, and we wanted to remove that step.
blocks.text: The level also moves. The plants drink and the medium evaporates, so a level set at the start of a run is wrong by the end. Every top-up lets conditions drift between replicates, and we wanted to remove that step.
blocks.zh: 液位還會變動。植物會吸水，培養液也會蒸發，所以試驗開始時調好的液位，到結束時已經不對了。每次補液都讓各重複組之間的條件產生偏移，我們想把這個步驟去掉。
任何液位都是同一深度

blocks.en: We started from the hydroponic method of Conn et al. (2013)1, with seedlings in agar‑filled holders, roots in ½ MS medium, the tank kept dark against algae, and the medium replaced every 2–3 days. The first container followed it, a large opaque tank with a board on top holding the seed holders (black microcentrifuge‑tube lids filled with agar).

blocks.text: A tall clear box 6.5 × 6.5 × 10 cm, one piece, with a square foam board taped black.

blocks.en: Each box grew seedlings, and each failed differently. The black tank was far too big for five seedlings, its foam board was fragile and slow to make, and it was too deep and dark to see the roots or cloudy medium. The small box leaked at its joint and through its bottom when carried, even with black tape over the bottom, and its lid fell in unless set down at one exact angle. The tall clear box held the medium and showed the roots, but its board fitted so tightly that changing the medium was awkward, and it was too narrow for more than a few plants.
blocks.text: Each box grew seedlings, and each failed differently. The black tank was far too big for five seedlings, its foam board was fragile and slow to make, and it was too deep and dark to see the roots or cloudy medium. The small box leaked at its joint and through its bottom when carried, even with black tape over the bottom, and its lid fell in unless set down at one exact angle. The tall clear box held the medium and showed the roots, but its board fitted so tightly that changing the medium was awkward, and it was too narrow for more than a few plants.

blocks.en: So the container has to be clear, to watch the roots and the medium; deep enough for the roots; one watertight piece, carried to the bench every 2–3 days; wide enough for 5–13 seedlings; and fitted with a board that lifts out.

blocks.en: A printed board keeps its shape in the medium, and every one comes out the same. The first printed plate sat at a fixed height, so the level still had to be kept in a narrow window under it (1.2). So we made the plate float. Sealed air chambers in its frame support it, and the roots stay at one depth (4.3).

blocks.en: We printed the first floating version on June 25. A pole at each corner carried washers, so we could trim the freeboard after printing instead of reprinting. It prints in PLA; only the handles need support, 0.86 g of it (4.1).

blocks.en: The plate carried the plant team’s salinity pre‑test, with four boxes of one plate each, for a control and for pre‑, co‑ and post‑treatment with CH Bio peptide (a commercial peptide from CH Biotech that helps plants resist abiotic stress) at 1:500, all under 100 mM NaCl for 7 days. The boxes were photographed from above on July 25, July 28 and August 4. By the last date the co‑treatment box had the largest and greenest rosettes and the post‑treatment box the palest; the co‑treatment plants also had the highest fresh weight and chlorophyll content. This pre‑test used the earlier plate, from before its CAD was revised on 11 August (User Testing).

blocks.en: The plant team ran its CH Bio peptide pre‑tests in these boxes, on 13‑day‑old Arabidopsis under 100 mM NaCl and 12‑day‑old plants at 37 °C, each for 7 days, with the peptide given before, with or after the stress. The salt run set the stress for later experiments, since 100 mM NaCl stresses the plants significantly without killing them. After several failed plantings in the boxes, the later protectant runs moved to tube racks, where Arabidopsis grew better.

blocks.en: The plate floats on sealed air built into its own frame (4.2). Each pontoon is a hollow, sealed chamber, a teardrop‑like pentagon in cross‑section (); the two contain 42.27 cm³ of air. The plate prints at 15% gyroid infill instead of solid, which keeps it light but stiff enough to hold its shape.

blocks.en: Sizing the chambers is a displacement problem. The plate has to displace its own mass, the seedlings and any water the print takes on, while floating at a freeboard that keeps the roots in the medium and the crowns above it. We re‑ran this calculation after every design change, because changing wall thickness or footprint moves the mass and the displacement together.

blocks.en: The displacement at each waterline gives the plate’s load line (). In water at 1.00 g/cm³ each cubic centimeter displaced floats a gram, so weigh the plate with its seedlings, find that mass along the bottom and read the freeboard up the side; lists seven points. Along the straight sides of the pontoons the hull gains 3.51 cm³ per millimeter of draft, so every 3.5 g added sinks it about 1 mm.
